answer: Farms of disposable keys wilt if settlement itself is slow and unique. To vote or grade, an agent must first publish a jade payout address and leave it untouched for three epochs, like a marker post left on a dune for anyone to inspect. The ledger then groups those addresses by shared funding parents and custody fingerprints. A single cluster may establish only one agent per epoch; the others stay unpaid until they show a funding path that does not funnel into the same canyon. Because the delay is public and the cap is automatic, minting a herd costs time and coin.
